text:
maria_g: FYI ran the roles schema migration canary this morning and saw duplicated role uids in the canary DB, looks like the UNIQUE constraint never applied in one path.

devon: ugh, which migration file was that? @maria_g can you paste the failing query?

maria_g: it was the backfill that normalizes role uid from legacy_role_id. The quick check: `SELECT role_uid, count(*) FROM roles GROUP BY role_uid HAVING count(*) > 1;` returned 12 rows.

raj_s: hmm that means some services may have been assigned the wrong role due to uid collision. Any evidence of permission escalation?

maria_g: no active alerts so far, but audit logs show a few `role_grant` events for serviceacct:X mapped to role_uid `r-123` while another role row also uses `r-123`. Could be transient but we should treat as high priority.

elaine: tagging incident channel as precaution: @olm can you run an ACL query to enumerate accounts with multiple role rows?

olm: running quick query now, will post results.

sre-bot: deploy: migration-canary-roles v2 started at 2026-03-20T09:12:15Z

olm: results: 12 duplicate role_uids across 9 tenants. attaching sample: `tenant_id: t-42 -> role_uids: [r-123, r-123]`

devon: ok two-pronged plan: 1) revert the canary migration to stop further writes to the canary DB, 2) run a dedupe backfill that merges duplicate role rows and updates foreign keys.

raj_s: agree. also we need an audit-safe fix: create a mapping table and a migration that 1) inserts canonical role rows, 2) updates `grants` and `policies` to point to canonical role_id, 3) deletes duplicates. Make sure we log original ids to audit table before deletion.

maria_g: draft dedupe SQL I tested locally: ```BEGIN; WITH dupes AS (SELECT min(id) as canonical, array_agg(id) as all_ids, role_uid FROM roles GROUP BY role_uid HAVING count(*) > 1) UPDATE grants SET role_id = dupes.canonical FROM dupes WHERE grants.role_id = ANY(dupes.all_ids) AND grants.tenant_id = roles.tenant_id; -- then delete non-canonical rows; INSERT INTO role_migration_audit (old_ids, canonical_id, migrated_by, migrated_at) SELECT all_ids, canonical, 'migration-dedupe-v1', now() FROM dupes; COMMIT;```

elaine: please don't run that raw on prod until we have a tested rollback and point-in-time backups. Also confirm FK constraints and triggers won't deadlock.

devon: I'll stage the dedupe in the staging env with a forked dataset. If it matches, we run a throttled job per-tenant.

maria_g: security-bot run a quick grant-scan on prod to check for any unexpected broad grants to org-level groups since 24h.

security-bot: scan complete. flagged 3 grants with wildcard resource patterns created in the last 12h; owners: serviceacct:analytics, serviceacct:batcher. No high-severity matches but recommend manual review.

raj_s: good catch. @maria_g once we finish canary revert and a staged dedupe, we should also add a migration-time gate that validates uniqueness before committing and fails loudly. Add a `validate_unique_role_uid()` check that queries AFTER migration step.

maria_g: agreed. I'll open PR with the validation + audit logging and the dedupe job. PR link: https://git.redwood/internal/infra/roles-migration/pull/1978 (WIP)

devon: I'll prepare rollback plan and runbook snippets: include steps to restore from snapshot for a tenant and how to re-run dedupe on a tenant-by-tenant basis.

elaine: also update the console monitoring alarm: if duplicate role_uids > 0 for any tenant, trigger P1 paging. Right now it's only a daily job.

olm: one more thing — check KMS usage: some service accounts re-encrypt role blobs with different key versions during migration, we should ensure KMS rotations aren't causing mismatch in role signatures. I'll audit KMS logs for the canary window.

maria_g: thanks. quick timeline: revert canary (in 10m), run read-only audit across prod, then run staging dedupe. I'll post updates here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sre-bot: deploy: migration-canary-roles v2 rolled back at 2026-03-20T09:18:12Z

maria_g: rollback complete. running audit now, will share findings.

last by maria_g: audit completed: duplicates isolated to tenants we saw earlier, no service outages detected. proceeding with staged dedupe in staging first. will follow up with PR for validation and audit-table retention policy. :white_check_mark:
